item.description: arXiv:2506.12774v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P$ be a polytope defined by the system $A x \leq b$, where $A \in R^{m \times n}$, $b \in R^m$, and $\text{rank}(A) = n$. We give a short geometric proof of the following tight upper bound on the number of vertices of $P$: $$ n! \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\text{average}}} \cdot \text{vol}(B_2) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi n}} \cdot \left(\frac{2 \pi}{e}\right)^{n/2} \cdot n^{n/2} \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\text{average}}}, $$ where $\Delta$ is the maximum absolute value of $n \times n$ subdeterminants of $A$, and $\Delta_{\text{average}}$ is the average absolute value of subdeterminants of $A$ corresponding to a triangulation of $P$'s normal fan. Assuming that $A$ is integer, such polyhedra are called $\Delta$-modular polyhedra. Note that in the integer case, the bound can be simplified via the inequality $\Delta_{\text{average}} \geq \Delta_{\min} \geq 1$, where $\Delta_{\min}$ is the minimum absolute value of subdeterminants of $A$ corresponding to feasible bases of $A x \leq b$. For this, we prove and use a symmetric variant of Macbeath's theorem. Additionally, we give a direct argument based on prior results in the field, showing that the graph diameter of $P$ is bounded by $O\bigl(n^3 \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\min}} \cdot \ln (n \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\min}}) \bigr)$. Thus, both characteristic of $P$ are linear in $\Delta/\Delta_{\min}$. From an algorithmic perspective, we demonstrate that: Given $A \in Q^{m \times n}$, $b \in Q^m$, and an initial feasible solution to $A x \leq b$, the convex hull of $P$ can be constructed in $O(n)^{n/2} \cdot m^2 \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\text{average}}}$ operations. For simple polyhedra, the dependence on $m$ reduces to linear; Given $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ and $b \in Q^m$, the number $|P \cap Z^n|$ can be computed in $O(n)^n \cdot \frac{\Delta^4}{\Delta_{\text{average}}}$ arithmetic operations.
item.dc:creator: Bludov Mikhail, Gribanov Dmitry, Klimenko Maxim, Kupavskii Andrey, L\'angi Zsolt, Rogozin Alexander, Voronov Vsevolod

item.title: Ehrhart non-positivity and unimodular triangulations for classes of s-lecture hall simplices
item.description: arXiv:2508.18890v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Counting lattice points and triangulating polytopes is a prominent subject in discrete geometry, yet proving Ehrhart positivity or existence of unimodular triangulations remain of utmost difficulty in general, even for ``easy'' simplices. We study these problems for classes of s-lecture hall simplices. Inspired by a question of Olsen, we present a new natural class of sequences s for which the s-lecture hall simplices are not Ehrhart positive, by explicitly estimating a negative coefficient. Meanwhile, motivated by a conjecture of Hibi, Olsen and Tsuchiya, we extend the previously known classes of sequences s for which the s-lecture hall simplex admits a flag, regular and unimodular triangulation. The triangulations we construct are explicit.
item.dc:creator: Jhon B. Caicedo, Martina Juhnke, Germain Poullot

item.title: A combinatorial description of when a self-associated set of points fails to be arithmetically Gorenstein
item.description: arXiv:2512.16766v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a combinatorial proof that the set of points associated to a self-dual code with no proportional columns is arithmetically Gorenstein if and only if the code is indecomposable. This answers a question asked by Toh\u{a}neanu. We do so by providing a combinatorial way to compute the dimension of the Schur square of a self-dual code through a zero-one symmetrization of a systematic generator matrix. Our approach also allows us to compute the Gorenstein defect. As a consequence, we obtain a combinatorial characterization of arithmetically Gorenstein self-associated sets of points over an algebraically closed field. We also show that, for any finite field, almost all self-dual codes of large length are indecomposable, and hence their associated sets of points are arithmetically Gorenstein.
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo Rodr\'iguez-Pajares, Diego Ruano, Flavio Salizzoni

item.title: Analytical properties of $q$-metallic numbers
item.description: arXiv:2604.19898v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an integer $n\geq 1$, consider the $n$-th metallic number $\phi_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$ (e.g. $\phi_1$ is the golden number) and denote by $[\phi_n]_q$ its $q$-deformation in the sense of S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko. This is an algebraic continued fraction which admits an expansion into a power series $[\phi_n]_q =\sum_{l=0}^{+\infty} \kappa_l(\phi_n) q^l$ around $q=0$, with integral coefficients. By using techniques from analytic combinatorics, we establish several properties of the sequence $( \kappa_l(\phi_n))_{l\geq 0}$ of Taylor coefficients: characterisation by recurrences or by differential equations, closed-form expressions when $n=1,2,3$, and asymptotics. We also present some remarkable identities induced by the action of the modular group $PSL(2,Z)$ and address, mainly through computer experimentations, the question of the logarithmic behaviour of the sequence $( \kappa_l(\phi_n))_{l\geq 0}$. A particular accent is put on the comparison between the $q$-deformation $[\phi_1]_q$ of the golden ratio and RNA secondary structures, the former being actually a signed version of the latter. By doing so, we would be pleased to bring the interest of combinatoricians to the newly discovered world of $q$-numbers.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Pedon

item.title: Improved Lower Bounds on Tree Covers
item.description: arXiv:2607.27264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A tree cover of an $n$-point metric space is a collection of $k$ trees such that every pairwise distance is approximately preserved in at least one tree. For fixed $k$, the best known distortion upper bound is $\tilde{O}(n^{1/k})$ and the best known lower bound is $\Omega_k(n^{1/2^{k-1}})$. In this paper, we prove a lower bound of $\Omega_k(n^{1/(k-1)^2})$ for all $k\ge 3$, significantly narrowing the gap towards the upper bound. Our approach makes use of a novel algebraic topological notion that we call the \emph{agreement index}: the equivariant topological index of a simplicial complex encoding pairwise agreement among tree labels. This notion helps characterize the power and limit of algebraic and topological methods for analyzing tree covers, and we believe it will also find applications to other problems.
item.dc:creator: Yu Chen, Shengtang Huang, Zihan Tan, Hangyu Xu

item.title: Complexity of Arc-Decompositions involving Perfect Matchings and Cycle Factors
item.description: arXiv:2608.24031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For two digraph properties $P_1$ and $P_2$, a $(P_1,P_2)$-arc-decomposition of a digraph $D$ is a partition $A(D)=A_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}A_2$ such that the spanning subdigraphs $D[A_1]$ and $D[A_2]$ have properties $P_1$ and $P_2$, respectively. We prove that it is NP-complete to decide whether a digraph admits an arc-decomposition with properties $(P_1,P_2)$ where $(P_1,P_2)\in \{$(perfect matching, having no odd cycle), (perfect matching, strong), (perfect matching, having an out-branching), (cycle factor, having no odd cycle)$\}$. All four problems remain NP-complete even when restricted to strongly connected digraphs. We also prove that every strongly connected digraph with minimum semi-degree at least three contains two vertex-disjoint cycles whose simultaneous arc deletion leaves the digraph strongly connected. These results settle some open problems posed by Bang-Jensen, Bessy, Gon\c{c}alves, and Picasarri-Arrieta [Theoret. Comput. Sci. 928 (2022), 167--182].
item.dc:creator: Hangning Liu, J{\o}rgen Bang-Jensen, Jin Yan, Jia Zhou

item.title: Stable Symmetric Series, Differential Operators, and Jack Deformations
item.description: arXiv:2608.25651v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce stable symmetric series which encode normalized conjugacy classes and their multiplication operators simultaneously for all symmetric groups. This gives a direct route from the Ivanov--Kerov algebra to shifted symmetric functions and to differential operators in $U(\mathcal W_{1+\infty})$. Using the Goulden--Jackson product, we extend the construction to Jack polynomials, recover shifted Jack eigenvalues and Pieri-type relations, and obtain explicit candidate operators in degrees three and four. Their real and quaternionic specializations to zonal polynomials are verified by Gaussian matrix integrals and exhaustive Wick enumeration.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Yves Thibon

item.title: On a classical zero-sum invariant II: Disproof of a long-standing conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.17127v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, let $\nu(G)$ be the smallest {nonnegative} integer $\ell$ such that every zero-sum free sequence $T$ over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ has the following property: all nonzero elements of $G$ that do not occur as a subsequence sum of $T$ lie in a proper coset of some subgroup of $G$. It is easy to check that $\mathsf d (G)-1 \le \nu (G) \le \mathsf d (G)$, where $\mathsf d (G)$ is the small Davenport constant of $G$. A conjecture by Gao from the year 2000 stated that equality should always hold at the lower bound. This conjecture has since been confirmed for many families of groups (including all p-groups and groups of rank at most two). In this paper, we disprove the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Alfred Geroldinger, Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: There Are No Nontrivial Perfect Codes in the Johnson Scheme
item.description: arXiv:2609.23128v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In his seminal work from 1973, Delsarte conjectured that the Johnson schemes admit no nontrivial perfect codes. We prove this fundamental conjecture which is central in combinatorial coding theory. Our arguments combine lower bounds on the design strength of a perfect code with divisibility conditions for the size of a metric ball. We show that the ball size divides the greatest common divisor of specified binomial coefficients. An exact formula for this gcd implies squarefreeness and localizes a power of each prime divisor of the ball size to a short interval. Lloyd polynomials, explicit prime estimates, and bounds for linear forms in logarithms then exclude all sufficiently large radii. Additional arithmetic arguments handle the remaining radii.
item.dc:creator: Tuvi Etzion, Xiande Zhang, Wenjie Zhong

item.title: Upper $k$-Star-Forming Sets, $k$-Independence, and Upper Domination
item.description: arXiv:2610.03785v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $\beta_k(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing maximum degree less than $k$, and let $SF_k(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a minimal $k$-star-forming set. The known inequality $\beta_k(G)\le SF_k(G)$ suggests asking when equality holds. We place this question in the framework of upper domination: at $k=1$, $\beta_1(G)=\alpha(G)$ and $SF_1(G)=\Gamma(G)$, so the classical equality $\Gamma=\alpha$ on bipartite graphs is exactly the first member of the proposed hierarchy. We prove the equality for complete bipartite graphs for every $k$, obtaining \[ \beta_k(K_{a,b})=SF_k(K_{a,b})=\max\{a,b,2k-2\}\qquad(a,b\ge k), \] and record the elementary low-degree case $\Delta(G)<k$. For $k=2$ we derive certificate restrictions for minimal $2$-star-forming sets in bipartite graphs. For chain graphs we go further: we prove $\beta_2(G)=SF_2(G)$ and obtain an exact formula for their common value. The proof uses the nested-neighborhood structure together with a classification of witnesses to the indispensability of a high internal-degree vertex. We retain the equality problem for chain graphs as a conjecture only for $k\ge3$, and formulate the broader bipartite conjecture. We also determine the upper domination number of every rectangular grid and combine it with the known exact dissociation number to compare $\Gamma$, $\beta_2$, and $SF_2$. In particular, $\Gamma=\beta_2$ on every even-by-even rectangular grid, while $\beta_2\le SF_2$ always; this motivates a grid equality conjecture whose even-by-even case would yield a three-parameter identity.
item.dc:creator: Rafik Sahbi

item.title: Total eight-colorings of maximal planar graphs of maximum degree six
item.description: arXiv:2610.32717v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every finite simple maximal planar graph of maximum degree at most six admits a total eight-coloring. We first show that every proper vertex four-coloring of a subcubic graph extends to a total five-coloring. A curvature inequality for boundary walks then gives a matching decomposition of four-connected triangulations with degrees five and six, extending their prescribed vertex four-colorings to total eight-colorings. In a minimum counterexample, two local boundary colorings force the degree-four vertices to have disjoint neighborhoods. A characterization of the local extension obstructions permits these vertices to be restored simultaneously. The proof uses Hamiltonian-connectedness of four-connected planar graphs and Kardo\v{s}'s Hamiltonicity theorem for three-connected cubic planar graphs.
item.dc:creator: Enqiang Zhu

item.title: Two families of Young tableaux with periodic walls: Counting formulas and differential transcendence
item.description: arXiv:2610.35067v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Banderier, Marchal, and Wallner studied the enumeration problem for Young tableaux with walls. These are similar to standard Young tableaux, except that local decreases are allowed at some walls. In 2021, Banderier and Wallner counted Young tableaux with periodic walls, in which the elementary blocks are Young diagrams of shape $(2,2)$. They obtained exact counting formulas for $30$ of the $32$ classes up to symmetry. In this paper, we first derive recurrences for counting the remaining two classes of Young tableaux with periodic walls. We then prove that their counting exponential generating functions are differentially transcendental. Consequently, they are neither D-algebraic nor D-finite. This disproves a conjecture of Banderier and Wallner.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Jiahang Liu, Guoce Xin

item.title: On the facets of the Cayley polytope of Stanley's triangulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Disjunctions over the cells of a triangulation arise in formulations of piecewise-linear functions. For a poset $P$ on $[d]$, we study the convex hull $D$ of the simplices of Stanley's triangulation of the order polytope of $P$, each lifted by its own indicator vector. Via the Cayley trick, for any disjunction of full-dimensional polytopes, the facets of the convex hull other than those described by the bounds on the indicator variables correspond to the facet normals of the Minkowski sum of the polytopes, and each is described by the full optimal big-M lifting of the supporting inequality with that normal of any one polytope. For Stanley's triangulation, with $M(P)$ the Minkowski sum of its simplices, lifting only the facet-describing inequalities of the simplices need not suffice, unlike some other cases; we show that it suffices if and only if $M(P)$ is alcoved, if and only if deleting one element of $P$ leaves a chain. Otherwise, the coefficients of the additional facet-describing inequalities are governed by the least number $\ell(P)$ of elements whose deletion leaves a chain: for fixed $\ell(P)$, the largest entry of a primitive facet normal grows like $d^{\ell(P)-1}$, and it can be exponential in $d$ if $\ell(P)$ grows with $d$. For $d \geq 3$ and $\ell(P)\leq2$ the sharp bound is $d-2$.
item.dc:creator: Yushan Qu, Jon Lee

item.title: Facet normals of Minkowski sums of staircase simplices
item.description: arXiv:2610.35689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Staircase simplices are the simplices of the standard (Freudenthal--Kuhn) triangulation of $[0,1]^d$ and of Stanley's triangulations of order polytopes. We study the facet normals of their Minkowski sums and how the number of summands constrains the size of primitive integer normals. We characterize the normals attainable with a prescribed number of summands in terms of $d-1$ linearly independent zero-one vectors orthogonal to the normal, whose supports have an intersection graph that can be colored with one color per summand. This gives a combinatorial characterization of the least number of summands needed to realize a normal. For two summands, all primitive normals have entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, and we determine which of them occur. For three summands we bound every entry in absolute value by $3^{(d-2)/3}$ and construct normals with entries of order $\theta^d$, $\theta$ the plastic number; for four summands a second construction gives entries of order $\psi^d$, $\psi$ the supergolden ratio. Since $\psi>3^{1/3}$, the largest coefficients for three and four summands are exponentially separated. For vectors with at most two distinct nonzero entry values, we determine the least number of summands exactly, using a matching-rank formula proved by exterior algebra and representations of symmetric groups. With no restriction on the number of summands, the maximum coefficient equals the classical maximum for facets of $0/1$-polytopes in the same dimension.
item.dc:creator: Yushan Qu, Jon Lee

item.title: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ for even $n$: rigid sequences, products, and growth beyond Harborth's bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.35819v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ and $\eta(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. For even $n$, Harborth's construction gives $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+1$, with equality when $n$ is a power of two. Wang and Zeng recently showed that this bound is strict for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n$ that is not a power of two, with an excess of $2^{r-3}(m-1)$, where $m$ is the odd part of $n$; this disproves Properties C and D. We show that the excess grows faster than $2^r$. For every even $n=2^am$ with odd $m\ge3$ and every $r\ge4$, \[ s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+(m-1)\,2^{r-3}\lfloor r/4\rfloor+1 , \] so that $s(C_n^r)-2^r(n-1)\ge c_n\,r\,2^r$.
item.dc:creator: Christian Elsholtz

item.title: Interactive Particle Systems on Hypergraphs, Drift Analysis and the WalkSAT algorithm
item.description: arXiv:1909.12353v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze the expected running time of WalkSAT, a well-known local search procedure for satisfiability solving, on satisfiable instances of the k-XOR SAT problem. We obtain estimates of this expected running time by reducing the problem to a setting amenable to classical techniques from drift analysis. A crucial ingredient of this reduction is the definition of (new, explosive) hypergraph versions of interacting particle systems, notably of coalescing and annihilating random walks as well as the voter model. The use of these tools allows to show that the expected running time of WalkSAT depends on structural parameter (we call odd Cheeger drift) of the dual of the formula hypergraph.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Istrate, Cosmin Bonchis, Mircea Marin

item.title: Polynomial and Hyperplane Avoidance over the Integers with Applications to Integer-Point Counting
item.description: arXiv:2411.07030v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the \emph{Polynomial Avoidance Problem}: given a finite collection $F \subseteq Z[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of nonzero polynomials, find a vector $x \in Z^n$ of minimum $\ell_p$-norm such that $f(x)\neq0$ for every $f \in F$. Each polynomial is given sparsely as a list of its nonzero terms. The affine special case is the \emph{Hyperplane Avoidance Problem}. This special case arises in Barvinok-type algorithms for counting integer points in polyhedra, when certain rational generating functions must be evaluated at a removable singularity. Our main results are as follows: 1) Let $D:=\sum_{f\in F} \text{deg} f$. Every instance admits a feasible vector $x$ satisfying \[ \|x\|_1 \leq \min\left\{D,\frac{D+n}{2}\right\}. \] This bound is tight. Such a vector can be found by a deterministic algorithm whose bit complexity is polynomial in $D$ and the sparse encoding length of the input. Our proof uses a new algorithmic variant of the \emph{Combinatorial Nullstellensatz}; 2) In the affine case, with $m$ input polynomials, such a vector can be constructed by a fast deterministic polynomial-time algorithm using $O(nm)$ arithmetic operations. For the homogeneous case, Barvinok's original approach provides only the weaker guarantee $\|x\|_1 = O((nm)^{n-1})$; 3) The problem is NP-hard for every $p\in R_{\geq 1}\cup\{\infty\}$, even for homogeneous linear forms; 4) As an application, we improve the complexity bound for counting integer points in general rational polytopes. We also improve the bound for polyhedra of bounded codimension; this includes the counting version of the \emph{Unbounded Subset-Sum} problem as a special case.
item.dc:creator: Grigorii Dakhno, Dmitry Gribanov, Nikita Kasianov, Anastasiia Kats, Andrey Kupavskii, Nikita Kuz'min, Stanislav Moiseev

item.title: Infinite unrestricted sumsets in subsets of abelian groups with large density
item.description: arXiv:2504.08649v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(G,+)$ be a countable abelian group such that the subgroup $\{g+g\colon g\in G\}$ has finite index and the doubling map $g\mapsto g+g$ has finite kernel. We establish lower bounds on the upper density of a set $A\subset G$ with respect to an appropriate F{\o}lner sequence, so that $A$ contains a sumset of the form $\{t+b_1+b_2\colon b_1,b_2\in B\}$ or $\{b_1+b_2\colon b_1,b_2\in B\}$, for some infinite $B\subset G$ and some $t\in G$. Both assumptions on $G$ are necessary for our results to be true. We also characterize the F{\o}lner sequences for which this is possible. Finally, we show that our lower bounds are optimal in a strong sense.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Charamaras, Ioannis Kousek, Andreas Mountakis, Trist\'an Radi\'c

item.title: An Unconditional Lower Bound for the Active-Set Method in Almost-Linear Programming
item.description: arXiv:2507.16648v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that, for every fixed $\epsilon\in(0,1]$, the active-set method requires exponentially many iterations in the worst case to maximize a convex objective of the form $(x_1)^{1+\epsilon}+\vec c^{\top}\vec x$ subject to linear constraints, regardless of the pivot rule used. Our lower bound therefore holds for objectives arbitrarily close to the linear case $\epsilon=0$, where the active-set method coincides with the simplex method and a lower bound for all pivot rules would constitute a major breakthrough. The special case $\epsilon=1$ yields a lower bound in convex quadratic maximization. This improves on the best previously known lower bound [IPCO 2025] requiring polynomial objectives of degree $\omega(\log d)$ in dimension $d$ and firmly resolves the open question of whether a constant degree suffices. Our result is based on a novel extended formulation, recursively constructed using deformed products. Its key feature is that it projects onto a polygonal approximation of a parabola while preserving all of its exponentially many vertices. We define a convex objective with a single non-linear variable that forces the active-set method to follow the parabolic boundary of this projection, without allowing any shortcuts along chords corresponding to edges of its full-dimensional preimage.
item.dc:creator: Eleon Bach, Yann Disser, Sophie Huiberts, Nils Mosis

item.title: Combinatorial foundations for solvable chaotic local Euclidean quantum circuits in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2512.03029v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a graph-theoretic problem motivated by questions in quantum computing concerning the propagation of information in quantum circuits. A graph $G$ is said to be a bounded extension of its subgraph $L$ if they share the same vertex set, and the graph distance $d_L(u, v)$ is uniformly bounded for edges $uv\in G$. Given vertices $u, v$ in $G$ and an integer $k$, the geodesic slice $S(u, v, k)$ denotes the subset of vertices $w$ lying on a geodesic in $G$ between $u$ and $v$ with $d_G(u, w) = k$. We say that $G$ has bounded geodesic slices if $|S(u, v, k)|$ is uniformly bounded over all $u, v, k$. We call a graph $L$ geodesically directable if it has a bounded extension $G$ with bounded geodesic slices. Contrary to previous expectations, we prove that $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is geodesically directable. Physically, this provides a setting in which one could devise exactly-solvable chaotic local quantum circuits with non-trivial correlation patterns on 2D Euclidean lattices. In fact, we show that any bounded extension of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is geodesically directable. This further implies that all two-dimensional regular tilings are geodesically directable.
item.dc:creator: Fredy Yip

item.title: Unimodular random ideal hyperbolic polyhedra: geometric characteristics and random walks
item.description: arXiv:2601.14909v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate a systematic study of unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra in three-dimensional hyperbolic space, developing a geometric and probabilistic theory of their global behavior. At the heart of this theory is an intrinsic geometric characteristic, determined entirely by the dihedral angles surrounding a polyhedral face. We establish a unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity and show that the expectation of this local geometric invariant completely determines the global conformal type: under suitable assumptions, a random ideal polyhedron is almost surely parabolic precisely when the expected characteristic vanishes, and hyperbolic precisely when it is negative. This provides a sharp geometric classification of random infinite ideal polyhedra. Building on the correspondence with ideal circle patterns, we further develop a refined Ring Lemma that yields quantitative geometric control without bounded-degree assumptions. Combining these geometric tools with unimodular probability methods, we identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Together, these results establish a local-to-global framework linking intrinsic dihedral geometry, conformal uniformization, and stochastic behavior at infinity for unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra.
item.dc:creator: Huabin Ge, Yangxiang Lu, Chuwen Wang, Tian Zhou

item.title: From Global Optimization to Exact Coordinates: Heilbronn's Triangle Problem on the Unit Square Using Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2603.11107v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) approach for the Heilbronn triangle problem on the unit square. The formulation exploits the boundary structure of optimal configurations, which we establish rigorously, to fix coordinates and orientation variables a priori. With this formulation, a general-purpose global solver solves the case $n=9$ to global optimality within its numerical tolerances in about eight minutes on a laptop and without any precomputation, compared with about 23 hours of total computation for the best previous approach. The same model also solves $n=10$ for the first time, in under seven hours, and confirms the configuration of Comellas and Yebra (2002). The numerical solutions then guide an exact symbolic reconstruction, and the minimum triangle area of every reconstructed configuration is verified in exact arithmetic. This yields exact coordinates for all $n\le 10$, including the configurations of Comellas and Yebra (2002) for $n=9$ and $n=10$, together with rigorous lower bounds. Finally, we derive structural properties of optimal configurations, formulate a conjecture on the number of critical triangles, and pose an open question. All code and data are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Sudermann-Merx

item.title: On aggregation-quantization permutability problem for discrete-time Markov chains
item.description: arXiv:2603.14269v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given random walk on a graph, the corresponding discrete-time quantum walk can be constructed using the method proposed by Szegedy. On the other hand, given a partition of the set of states of a Markov chain, one can study the corresponding aggregated process. We extend the aggregation technique to the level of quantum Markov chains. We provide conditions under which application of these two operations - Szegedy's quantization and aggregation - give the same result. These consist of the strong lumpability of the underlying Markov chain supplemented by nonlinear relations, generalizing Kolmogorov's cycle condition, that account for the coefficients of both the original and the aggregated transition matrices. In particular, we show that the conditions are satisfied in the case of the random walk on graphs equipped with equitable partitions. We present several examples, which include the classical/quantum walks on Platonic solids. We discuss also relation of discrete-time classical/quantum walks on $N$-dimensional hypercube and the Ehrenfests urn model with $N$ particles. We apply our technique for of discrete-time walks on Cayley graphs of free groups. We also compare our results with those obtained using Cantero-Moral-Velazquez uniformization of unitary matrices.
item.dc:creator: Adam Doliwa, Artur Siemaszko, Adam Zalewski

item.title: Properties of the $\mathcal V$-Monoid of Weighted Leavitt Path Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.31087v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a row-finite weighted graph $(E,w)$, Preusser showed that the monoid $\mathcal{V}(L_k(E,w))$ of finitely generated projective modules over the weighted Leavitt path algebra $L_k(E,w)$ is isomorphic to a combinatorially defined weighted graph monoid $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$. We study two structural properties of $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$: confluence and cancellativity. We introduce a reduction system on the free commutative monoid presenting $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$, obtain sufficient conditions for non-confluence by constructing explicit non-confluent triples, and provide a complete confluence characterization for certain classes of weighted graphs. Turning to cancellativity, we work within Preusser's class of weighted graphs satisfying Condition (LPA), for which $L_k(E,w)$ is isomorphic to an unweighted Leavitt path algebra $L_k(F)$ via a two-step construction. We introduce an auxiliary graph associated to the intermediate step of this construction and use it to give a graph-theoretic characterization of when $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$ is cancellative. Finally, under Condition (LPA), we show that Preusser's construction upgrades to a graded isomorphism $L_k(E,w) \cong_{\operatorname{gr}} L_k(F)$ with respect to the standard $\mathbb{Z}^{\lambda(E,w)}$-grading of weighted Leavitt path algebras, yielding $\mathcal{V}^{\operatorname{gr}}(L_k(E,w)) \cong \mathcal{V}^{\operatorname{gr}}(L_k(F))$ as $\mathbb{Z}^{\lambda(E,w)}$-monoids.
item.dc:creator: Rishabh Goswami, Alfilgen Sebandal

item.title: On different notions related to APN mappings
item.description: arXiv:2609.22394v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An APN mapping $F:\mathbb{F}_{2^n}\to \mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ is a polynomial characterized by the non-vanishing property on 2-flats. In this work, we analyze notions that are closely related to this property. To understand which $k$-flats of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ remain flats under $F$, we study the $k$-breaking. The function $x^{-1}$ has been studied in the past in this context---we extend this study to general mappings and characterize the 2-breaking of APN functions. Recently, two generalizations of the APN property have been introduced: $k$-strongly non-normality and $k$-th-order sum-freedom. Sum-freedom generalizes the non-vanishing property of APN functions to higher dimensional flats. We provide in-depth observations of the relations between the breaking property, strongly non-normality and sum-freedom. We introduce a fourth concept called $k$-strongly breaking, which implies the breaking property. We derive several structural results for both notions and give a characterization of a subclass of APN functions in terms of the 2-strongly breaking property. We propose a different perspective of the non-vanishing property via a natural character transformation, which is closely related to the sum-of-square indicator of the components of $F$. We derive a precise value for the total sum of the sum-of-square indicators of $F$. With this approach, we provide a simple answer to Open Problem 4 in IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 52(9): 4160-4170, 2006. Moreover, it allows us to explore balancedness properties of polynomials, one of which characterizes component-wise APNness, for odd $n$, and provides a natural extension to any dimension. We show that Dillon's APN permutation and the Gold functions satisfy a related property, termed $k$-balanced, which is presented under our framework.
item.dc:creator: Ren\'e Rodr\'iguez-Aldama, Ajla \v{S}ehovi\'c, Enes Pasalic, Sadmir Kudin

item.title: Notes on a strongly aperiodic monotile in $E^3$
item.description: arXiv:2609.24779v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a clearer presentation of the Chair44 monotile, a new strongly aperiodic monotile in three-dimensional Euclidean space $E^3$.
item.dc:creator: Chaim Goodman-Strauss

item.title: Hull Games of Induced Path Convexities in Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.30302v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 1984, Frank Harary introduced the first convexity games in graphs, all of them based on the geodesic convexity, which is the graph convexity related to shortest paths. In 2024, Ara\'ujo et al. obtained the first PSPACE-hardness proofs on some of these geodesic games and generalized them to any graph convexity. In this paper, we investigate convexity games on several known induced path convexities: the monophonic $\mathrm{m}$-convexity and the $\ell_k$-convexities, based on induced paths and on induced paths of size at most $k$. We prove that the hull games $\mathrm{CHG}_{\mathrm{m}}$, $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ and their mis\`ere variants are PSPACE-complete for every $k\ge2$ even in graphs with diameter at most 3. We also use the Sprague-Grundy Theory to obtain a polynomial time algorithm to decide the winner of the games $\mathrm{CHG}_{\mathrm{m}}$ and $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ for any $k\ge2$ in disjoint unions of paths and cycles. For $k\ge3$ odd, we prove that Alice (1st player) wins $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ in the path $P_n$ if and only if $n$ is odd and she wins in the cycle $C_n$ if and only if $n=3$ or $n=\alpha\cdot (k+1)-1$ with $\alpha\ge2$. For $k\ge2$ even, the only periodic nimber sequences of $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ obtained through extensive computational testing occurred for $k=2^h-4$ with $h\ge3$, e.g, $k\in\{4,12,28,60,\ldots\}$. In this case ($k=2^h-4$ with $h\ge3$), we prove that the nimber sequences of $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ in $P_n$ and in $C_n$ are periodic and Alice loses (resp. wins) in $P_n$ (resp. $C_n$) with $n>k$ only when $n=3k+4$ (resp. $n\in\{2k+1,5k+3\}$). Finally, we show that, for $k=2$, the game $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_2}$ in paths $P_n$ is closely related to the classical game \emph{Couples-are-Forever} of J. H. Conway: it is still an open problem if the nimber sequence is periodic or not and Alice loses only for 12 values of $n$ up to $150$ million.
item.dc:creator: Eurinardo Costa, Leon Almeida, Rudini Sampaio

item.title: New Newton-type inequality and a unified perspective on Maclaurin's inequality via the inclusion relations of cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.28544v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The classical Newton-Maclaurin's inequalities for the elementary symmetric means are well known. In this paper, we derive a new class of Newton-type inequalities and generalize Maclaurin's inequality by connecting the elementary symmetric functions with their counterparts. Our idea is mainly motivated by the inclusion relations of G$\mathring{\text{a}}$rding's cones and $k$-convex cones.
item.dc:creator: Ning Cao, Xuanxuan Hu, Feida Jiang

item.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34378v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We count Boolean functions represented as the sign of a real polynomial of bounded degree on the $n$-dimensional cube. We prove that the logarithm of their number is asymptotic to that of the classical hyperplane-arrangement upper bound, uniformly over all degrees, with relative error $O((\log n)^2/n)$. We also obtain sharper additive and relative error estimates in particular degree ranges, including an additive error $O(n^2)$ between the logarithms throughout a small linear degree range and improved bounds just below the central degree. The proof combines probabilistic estimates for Reed--Muller codes with a deletion argument for sets of evaluation vectors, an entropy count, and a sharp-threshold estimate for expected rank deficiency.
item.dc:creator: Martin Anthony
